subject: Business Models
title: The Ad-Supported Downgrade
description: A 60-second lesson on The Ad-Supported Downgrade.

hook.text: Netflix introduced an ad-supported tier at $6.99. What used to be free from ads now costs $15.49.

buildup.text: Ad tiers let companies maintain subscriber counts while extracting double revenue: ads plus subscriptions.

discovery.text: Disney+ and HBO Max followed Netflix. The 'premium' tier is what the original subscription always was.

twist.text: Hulu launched with ads in 2008. The ad-free version came later at double the price. The reverse approach.

climax.text: Ad-supported tiers redefine 'premium' as 'the experience that used to be the default.'

punchline.text: Pay less, watch ads. Or pay more for what used to be included.

quiz.question: Why do streaming services add ad-supported tiers?
options: To extract revenue from both ads and subscriptions

details.summary: Ad-supported downgrades offer cheaper subscription tiers that include advertising, expanding the subscriber base at lower price points. Netflix, Disney+, and Spotify all offer ad-supported plans that generate revenue from both subscription fees and advertising simultaneously.
details.whyItMatters: Ad-supported tiers solve the subscriber growth ceiling by reaching price-sensitive consumers who would not pay full price. They generate dual revenue streams and provide an upsell path toward premium ad-free tiers over time.
takeaways: Lower-priced ad-supported tiers attract price-sensitive subscriber segments
Dual revenue from subscriptions and advertising maximizes ARPU
Ad tiers create an upsell path to premium ad-free subscriptions

faq.question: How profitable are ad-supported subscription tiers compared to premium?
faq.answer: Ad-supported tiers can actually generate higher total ARPU than premium tiers because they combine subscription fees with advertising revenue. Netflix's ad tier reportedly generates more revenue per user than its standard plan because ad revenue per viewer is substantial at premium ad rates.

faq.question: Why did Netflix and Disney+ add ad-supported tiers after years without them?
faq.answer: Subscriber growth in premium tiers plateaued in mature markets. Price-sensitive consumers would not pay full price. The advertising market offered billions in incremental revenue. Competitors with ad tiers were acquiring subscribers that Netflix and Disney+ were missing entirely.
